chunk_map.heading: # Map the gaps, cut the rule (title slide)
Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps
Read the contrast, push back where it generalises
Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed
Approve, unless the cut spreads past the one rule

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0 L7 'M5's session may still be running the re-send... decide whether it is done enough, should be stopped, or counts as the partial artefact' reads as first-mention inside the exercise, but the enclosing module's own '## Start here' (curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md L20-26) already establishes 'M5', 'the packaged Module 5 re-send', 'the un-packaged Module 4 send-off', and 'accept the partial session as the artefact' before this exercise's include position -- module-signposting-as-prior-context carve-out. Closest judgment call: chunk 4 L44 'Push back if the diff touches more than the one rule you flagged' reuses 'diff' (earlier chunks use it for the two-session comparison) for a second sense (the CLAUDE.local.md edit's diff); the immediate context -- the whole chunk is about approving the file edit just made -- disambiguates it as the edit's diff, not the session diff, so it stays inside the rule rather than vague-with-full-history.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only backward beat references in body are to Module 4 ('m4/<slug>' branch, task.md) and Module 5 ('m5/<slug>' branch, plan.md, the M5 worktree) -- both modules exist in the training and the module-set cross_module audit already PASSed the M4-M5-M6 arc (module maintainer block L78: 'cross_module @54577f39: PASS -- set=[run-the-first-experiment,learn-from-the-test,spot-gaps-build-the-loop]'). No 'the X you did/saw' phrasing pointing at a beat absent from the current set.

Shortest chunk is 4 ('Approve, unless the cut spreads past the one rule', L41-45): two full bullets, each a self-carrying instruction (approve the pause; push back if the edit over-reaches) -- not a bare wait-state or single context-dependent fragment. Every other chunk carries a bullet set plus a prompt block.

All four headers echo their own chunk content directly: chunk 1 'Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' -> bullets diff the sessions + prompt block ends 'Rank by damage-to-a-future-session'; chunk 3 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' -> body reads verbatim 'Ask Claude to cut the one rule the diagnosis killed'; chunk 4 'Approve, unless the cut spreads past the one rule' -> bullet 1 'If it asks, approve', bullet 2 'One rule cut, no more'. No header contradicted by its own content.

Checked all sub-items per chunk: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlative (L13 'The point: two sessions are enough to place every lesson' states a pedagogical thesis about the exercise's own two artefacts, not a value-prop claim about the exercise's quality -- also see maintainer L58 accept-note declining a §21 world-claim flag on this exact line, a sibling but distinct rule); no number-with-retraction pattern; no vague abstraction-noun stacks (L35 prompt's 'over-fitted verifier, plan.md staleness, reference-as-cage' name concrete failure shapes, not narrator abstraction); no verb triplets with an empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE '\b(surface|firing|compendium|forcing function|beat|mood|Connections)\b' against body (L1-45): no output. All body vocabulary (worktree, un-packaged/packaged, re-send, diagnosis, diff, verifier, plan.md, CLAUDE.local.md) is engineering-native or module-arc terminology already earned via M4/M5, not repo-authorial dialect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0's bold (**Time:**, **Session**, **What you do:**, **What you build:**, **The point:**) is the standard exercise-opener widget/label chrome exempted by this rule and confirmed by the file's own maintainer accept-note (L56: 'bullet leads plain; bold only on widget / label chrome, per ... check_slides.md §9'). Chunks 1-4 (the narrative bullets) carry zero bold -- grep -c '\*\*' on lines 17-45 -> 0. Well inside the <=1-per-slide budget.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File is curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md, rendered inside the module under the '.phase--exercise' wrapper the renderer keys on -- not prework/supplementary/reference (the shapes rule 10 warns get dropped). git diff 54577f39..HEAD on this file touches only sentence-level prose (punctuation, a header word swap, a 'Claude'->'the agent' substitution) -- no phase marker, tier marker, or content-flag change that could desync the two layouts. derive-body-view's signals report slide_count: 4, consistent with the four '##' chunks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md -> 'OK -- 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' grep -nE '\b(below|above|further down|at the top of this page|see below)\b' against the body: no hits (the one hit on 'below' in the file, L87 'Whole-room mood below 7', sits in the maintainer block, not the body).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size -- 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md -> 'files: 1  slides: 4  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets  oversized: 0 -- every slide is within limits.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is an exercise file, so all '##' headings should be imperative or phase labels: 'Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' / 'Read the contrast, push back where it generalises' / 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' / 'Approve, unless the cut spreads past the one rule' -- all four open on an imperative verb, none is a declarative law-claim mis-cast as a label.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every bullet supplies a concrete move, file/branch location, or predicted-model-behaviour tell (e.g. L28 predicts the four-dimension plan-summary opener and tells the student what to skim past; L43-44 gives the approve-then-verify-scope moves). Closest judgment calls: chunk 3 L34-35 'Rules-files have a half-life...' motivates the coming cut instruction with a first-use rationale rather than re-announcing doctrine already stated elsewhere in this file; chunk 4 L44 'One rule cut, no more' asserts an explicit scope priority (the boundary the student checks the diff against) rather than a content-free kicker restating the header. Both stay inside the rule.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: git diff 4e0370bc..HEAD on this file changes only bullet/prose text, no '##' heading line; maintainer block carries no provenance note of the '(from <old-file>, header ...)' shape. Neither trigger condition for this rule is present.

rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -noE '\[.*\]\(' on the body: no output (matches signals.has_urls: false). Body carries zero markdown links, so the cross-file-callback-by-position shape this rule targets does not occur. The M4/M5 references (chunk 0-1) name the source directly ('M5 worktree', 'm4/<slug> branch', 'task.md', 'plan.md') rather than locating it by position ('the previous module said'), so even read generously they don't trip this rule; that resolution sits under §1's carve-outs, not §2.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body -- this is a diagnose-and-diff exercise (compare two sessions, cut one rule), not a live-demo beat that narrates an outcome and then asks the student to guess it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering -- position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md -> 'OK -- 59 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent' (this file included, zero flagged). The maintainer block states 'Atomic -- no phase markers' and the body confirms it: no '## Phase N:' or '## N.' step headers exist anywhere in the file, so there is no content-ordinal numbering scheme for this rule to check.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: signals.has_urls: false; grep -noE '\[.*\]\(' on the body returns nothing. No in-body links of any kind (in-page anchor, external, or structural include) exist inside this file's own body for this rule to evaluate.

notes: Rule 17 ('a retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header') was excluded from my brief as prefill-resolved N/A even though this diff does rename chunk 4's header ('Say go' -> 'Approve'); I did not write a row for it per the brief's instruction, but note for the record that the new header is, if anything, better supported by the existing bullets ('If it asks, approve' now echoes 'Approve' directly), so no re-derivation was needed to trust the parked answer. Also outside slides scope: L29's swap of 'Claude' for 'the agent' (twice) while L22/L37 keep 'Claude' is a within-file naming inconsistency worth a writing-class look, though the referent stays unambiguous either way so it does not trip check_slides.md §1.
